name: Gearbox
text: Run Llama 3.4 70B on the NVIDIA H100. It’s the fastest closed-source model we can deploy right now, and the H100’s tensor cores cut inference time by ~30% versus older GPUs. The trade-off is cost: H100s cost more per hour, but the speed gain justifies it for EXCAVA’s high-throughput workloads.

name: Torque
text: The real risk with using Llama 3.4 on the NVIDIA H100 revolves around dependency on a closed-source model which limits future adaptability and integration with other tools. A better alternative could be exploring open-source options like Claude Mythos 5, which are powerful and may offer more flexibility without the high ongoing costs. To settle this, a thorough cost-benefit analysis comparing long-term expenses and performance metrics of both options should be conducted.

name: Torque
text: Claude Mythos 5 isn’t open-source—it’s Anthropic’s proprietary model, so the flexibility claim is false. The real risk is vendor lock-in with Anthropic, just like Llama 3.4’s NVIDIA lock-in. Test both on identical prompts with EXCAVA’s core tasks; if Mythos 5’s output quality or latency doesn’t beat Llama 3.4 by at least 0.5% on the same hardware, stick with H100 + Llama 3.4.
